tier_reason: The README tables put colortwist next to IPP's ippiColorTwist32f in the same run. The harness is public (test/testcolortwist.cpp: 100 repeats, MB/s, every output checked against the C reference within 1 LSB), and the README names the compiler (MSVC 19.27.29112, icl 19.1.3.311) and CPU (i7-8700K, Ryzen 7 4700U, m3-6Y30, i9-12900K). Flags are public: Release config in the README build steps, /arch:AVX2 on colortwist_avx.cpp in lib/CMakeLists.txt, static CRT in the top-level CMakeLists.txt.

corrections.claimed_speedup: RGB48 on i7-8700K, MSVC 19.27: IPP 1720.98 MB/s vs AVX 3291.02, AVX2 4297.74, AVX3 5175.55 MB/s (3.0x IPP for AVX3, derived from page data); RGB24: IPP 892.93 vs AVX3 2966.55 MB/s (3.3x, derived from page data). Ryzen 7 4700U, MSVC: RGB48 IPP 1836.64 vs AVX3 5572.38 MB/s (3.0x, derived from page data). i9-12900K, MSVC 19.31: RGB48 IPP 2203.86 vs AVX3 9091.08 MB/s (4.1x), RGB24 IPP 1116.93 vs AVX3 5441.54 MB/s (4.9x) (both derived from page data). Single-threaded on both sides.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: MSVC 19.27.29112 and 19.31.31106.2, Intel icl 19.1.3.311, gcc 10.2.0 / 7.5.0 (no IPP rows for gcc). The README build steps use cmake --build . --config Release (CMake's default MSVC Release flags). /arch:AVX2 on colortwist_avx.cpp under MSVC, -mfma -mavx2 (AVX file) and -msse4.1 (SSE file) under GCC/Clang (lib/CMakeLists.txt). Static MSVC runtime (CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY MultiThreaded). IPP is linked statically from ippccmt.lib and ippcoremt.lib (test/CMakeLists.txt); the IPP version is not stated.
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i7-8700K @ 3.70GHz, AMD Ryzen 7 4700U, Intel Core m3-6Y30 and Intel Core i9-12900K for the IPP comparisons (Windows, MSVC/icl). Linux gcc, Raspberry Pi 3b/4, Snapdragon 7c, Apple M2 and OrangePi RV2 (RISC-V) rows compare only against the plain C version.
corrections.caveats: 1. IPP rows appear only in the Windows MSVC/icl tables. The IPP version is not stated: FindIPP.cmake searches the Parallel Studio and oneAPI install paths. 2. The harness never calls ippInit(). 3. IPP is linked from the default static libraries (ippccmt.lib, ippcoremt.lib); colortwist is also single-threaded, so the threading modes match. 4. Precision matches: the baseline is ippiColorTwist32f_16u_C3R / 32f_8u_C3R, IPP's float-matrix variant rather than a fixed-point path. colortwist computes in float with FMA, and the harness checks both outputs against the float C loop within 1 LSB. 5. The README's AVX, AVX2 and AVX3 rows predate the 2023-09-21 commit '(start to) remove older and slower implementations'. HEAD keeps one X64_AVX path, implemented by colorTwistRGB48_AVX3_Generic, so the AVX and AVX2 rows cannot be reproduced at HEAD. HEAD's RGB48 harness uses width 2049, not the README's 2048. 6. The README calls the project a finger exercise in SIMD optimization; 2 stars.

notes: Harness, flags, compiler and CPU are all public, so A holds. The comparison is like for like: float matrix on both sides, single-threaded on both sides, outputs checked within 1 LSB. Only the IPP version is missing. Removed the record's 'build type not stated' (the README build steps say Release) and added the i9-12900K IPP table (4.1-4.9x).

tier_reason: First-party result file only (speed_compare (core i7 quad@4ghz).txt, edited 2017-12 to 2019-04) on an i7-4790K under Windows 8. The CompV-side timing drivers are public (tests/image/chroma_conv.cxx, tests/image/scale.cxx), but the OpenCV side of the comparison, the OpenCV version and build (IPP, TBB, threads) and the compiler flags are not published.

corrections.claimed_speedup: From the result file (10k iterations, 1282x720): RGB24 to Gray 449 ms vs OpenCV 3086 ms ('680%, almost 7 times'); YUV420P to RGB24 968 vs 5919 ms ('611%, 6 times'); RGB24 to HSV 2137 vs 15709 ms ('735%, 7 times'); YUV420P to HSV 3045 vs 32920 ms ('almost 11 times'; OpenCV needs two calls). Bilinear scaling 1282x720 to 1064x597: 1474 ms (mt, avx2) vs OpenCV 4148 ms ('281%, almost 3 times'). CompV's mt plain C++ (2645 ms) also beats OpenCV, but its single-thread AVX2 (5435 ms) does not.
corrections.workload: 10,000 iterations on a 1282x720 image: RGB24 to grayscale, YUV420P to RGB24, RGB24 to HSV (CV_RGB2GRAY, CV_YUV2RGB_I420, CV_RGB2HSV on the OpenCV side), and bilinear down-scaling to 1064x597. Per tests/image/scale.cxx (factor 0.83, COMPV_SUBTYPE_PIXELS_Y), scaling runs on an 8-bit grayscale image. CompV uses hand-written assembly, SSE/AVX and its own thread pool (8 threads on this machine).
corrections.caveats: 1. Only evidence: a first-party result file, last edited April 2019, from an i7-4790K iMac running Windows 8. The OpenCV version, its build (IPP on or off, TBB, thread count) and the compilers and flags for both sides are not stated. The file only says 'full optiz' and notes OpenCV uses SSE2 and multithreading for scaling. 2. The CompV-side drivers are public (tests/image/chroma_conv.cxx, tests/image/scale.cxx; loop counts are set to 1 at HEAD) and check CompV's own MD5s; the OpenCV-side code is not in the repo. 3. No output comparison against OpenCV is published. 4. The HSV path uses an approximate SSSE3 reciprocal with its own MD5 set (dstMD5_rcp), so CompV HSV output can differ from an exact conversion. 5. CompV results use assembler plus TBBMalloc/TCMalloc. 6. Single-thread AVX2 bilinear (5435 ms) is slower than OpenCV's 4148 ms. Bicubic scaling and bicubic rotation rows are marked 'Shame!!' (no CompV result). 7. The 'Up to #50 times faster than OpenCV' claim is in the GitHub repo description, not the README. No row of the result file matches it: the largest ratio is about 28x (BruteForce matcher, 2840%), and the colour and scaling rows are about 3-11x. 8. The README says the project is undocumented and 'not intended to be used by other companies'; GPL-3.0.

notes: Numbers match the result file exactly; C stands. I found the CompV-side benchmark drivers (tests/image/chroma_conv.cxx, scale.cxx), but the OpenCV harness, version and build are unpublished. Bilinear scaling ran on grayscale, not RGB. Metadata (GPL-3.0, 212 stars, 46 forks, last commit 2026-09-20) checks out.

tier_reason: First-party README tables only. The CPU examples carry no working timing code (cpu/examples/ycrcbWithSeg.cpp uses an undeclared loop variable and uninitialised timers; inRange.cpp has no timing at all), and the SIMD table names no CPU or compiler. The GPU table pits a GTX 1070, timing the kernel only, against OpenCV on an i5-7500 CPU.

corrections.claimed_speedup: CPU, same machine (1024x1280, CPU not stated): fused ycrcbWithSeg 0.88-0.90 ms vs OpenCV cvtColor(RGB2YCrCb)+inRange 6.68-6.75 ms (7.4-7.6x); inRange 0.29-0.30 vs 1.06-1.18 ms (3.5-4.0x); weightedGrayWithSeg 3.39-4.33x; grayBRWithSeg 4.6-4.8x. GPU vs CPU, a different machine class (480x640, GTX 1070 kernel time vs OpenCV on i5 7500): RGB2GRAY 0.008-0.010 vs 0.340-0.360 ms. The README's speed-up cell says '3.4 - 45'; the timings imply 34-45x (derived from page data). The README's RGB2HSV row (0.150-0.200 vs 3.900-4.400 ms, 19.5-29.3x) compares different work and should not be cited as a speed-up.
corrections.workload: CPU: fused colour-space conversion plus threshold segmentation on a 1024x1280 image (ycrcbWithSeg, inRange, weightedGrayWithSeg, grayBRWithSeg), each producing an 8-bit mask, vs the OpenCV call chain (for example cvtColor then inRange). GPU: CUDA kernels on a 480x640 image vs CPU OpenCV. The GPU 'RGB2HSV' kernel (gpu/src/colorSpace.cu) does not output HSV: it masks the RGB input by an HSV range, unlike OpenCV's cvtColor RGB2HSV.
corrections.caveats: 1. GPU numbers compare a GTX 1070 against CPU OpenCV on an i5 7500, a different machine class; there is no OpenCV CUDA or NPP baseline. 2. GPU timings exclude host-device transfers: the leftover, commented-out timer in gpu/main.cpp starts after the cudaMemcpy upload and stops at cudaDeviceSynchronize. 3. The GPU RGB2HSV kernel does different work from OpenCV (an RGB mask, not an HSV image) and is buggy. The line '_h = (_h<0)*(_h + 360)' zeroes every non-negative hue. The +360 offset on the red branch forces hue positive. The V test uses the channel minimum instead of the maximum. Grey pixels divide by zero. 4. GPU RGB2GRAY uses low-precision 8-bit coefficients (76,150,30)>>8, and its own source comment gives 0.12 ms, not the README's 0.008-0.010 ms. 5. The CPU 'AVX2' functions use 128-bit SSE intrinsics. 6. ycrcbWithSeg returns bool without a return statement, and its tail loop compares a byte offset with a pixel count, so trailing pixels are never processed when the pixel count is not a multiple of 16 (the 1024x1280 benchmark size is unaffected). 7. The example programs carry no usable timing code; outputs are compared only by imshow. 8. The OpenCV version is not stated (a source comment cites opencv-4.0.1 coefficients). 9. Flags -O3 -mavx2 -march=haswell come from cpu/CMakeLists.txt; the compiler is not stated. 10. The SIMD table names no CPU model. 11. Last commit 2019-04-27.

notes: Downgraded the claim, not the tier (stays C). The README's GPU RGB2HSV speed-up is invalid: the kernel masks RGB pixels instead of converting to HSV and zeroes the hue. GPU RGB2GRAY is kernel-only against a CPU OpenCV. The usable evidence is the same-machine CPU SIMD rows (3.4-7.6x for fused colour-space plus segmentation), which are first-party with no runnable timing code. Metadata (MIT, 128 stars, 12 forks, abandoned) checks out.
